stage1.impression: A careful night elevation of a shopfront. The lit room seen through the glass is the best thing in it: shelves, pendants, the counter and a stool, warm and believable. Everything outside the glass reads as CG. The neighbour is a flat, untextured stucco block with black holes for windows, the sidewalk is a smooth grey plane, the flats above are clean, unlit white trim, and nothing in the frame is blue, so it reads as a warm render rather than blue hour. The speaker is not the hero. All you see of it is a small pale driver in the vestibule, with no tint, and the frosted lightbox with the dancer is the brightest, biggest thing in the frame and reads as signage. Would a magazine run it as a specific place? Not yet. The dancer lightbox and the etched name make it specific, but the street around them makes it a generic visualisation.

blocking_9: A real blue-hour ambient: cool sky light on the street and facades so the warm room glows against blue-grey (exterior b_median > r_median)
The EARF speaker legible at a glance through the glass, with its tint and the light through its acrylic visible (speaker region lum_median >= 45)
The neighbour's blank stucco block either out of frame or given real detail (glazing, reflections, weathering)
Sidewalk with paving joints, staining and kerb wear instead of a smooth CG plane
Signs of life outside and above: a lit flat or two, a figure or a bike, so the street is not a stage set
The lightbox no brighter than the room behind the glass, so it reads as part of the shopfront and not a backlit poster
The door threshold reads as stone in light, not a flat, evenly lit slab

defects.what: The neighbour's facade is a flat, untextured stucco plane. Its upper window is a pure black hole with no glass or reflection, and the shutter has uniform CG slats. It measures warm (r61 g44 b35) where blue hour would make it cool.
Smooth, featureless sidewalk and kerb: no joints, gum spots, stains or texture. The reflections are clean blobs.
The flats above are clean, evenly lit white trim with no lit windows and no wear. They read as a model.
The frosted lightbox is the brightest broad area (median 94, against 22.5 for the room). It reads as a backlit poster or signage.
The etched EARF in the glass reads as pale letters floating or projected over the interior, not as etching catching light.
The door threshold is a flat, evenly lit slab (median 146, r193 g138 b84) with no texture. It looks like a lit plane.
The blackened-steel cladding shows a tile-like grid and glossy, flaky specular blotches. It reads as a mottled glazed tile rather than an even, sharp-edged steel patina.
The speaker seen through the vestibule is tiny and dark (median 23.5). It reads as a pale white driver with no smoked tint.
The interior is a single amber cast (b_median 3). Every surface goes orange, with no neutral concrete or timber.
A cut-off red object at the left frame edge, near the hydrant height. It is a distracting fragment.

changes.problem: There is no blue hour. The street and facades are warm grey and lit only by the 3000 K street lamps, so the warm room does not glow against a cool exterior.

evidence.measured: neighbour facade r_median 61, g 44, b 35; sidewalk [0,640,1200,800] r47 g35 b32: no channel goes cool anywhere

change.setting: sky / world ambient (blue-hour dome outside the street)
change.from: none (street lamps 3 x 150 W, 3000 K only)
change.to: a sky dome at about 9000 K, strength set so the neighbour facade sits at lum_median about 40; street lamps 150 W to 80 W

changes.expected: Facades and sidewalk go blue-grey, and the shop window becomes the warm focal point. The colour contrast does the work that exposure is doing now.

changes.problem: The grade's warm white balance pushes the whole frame to amber, so the interior has no neutral concrete or timber, and the exterior can never read as blue hour.
changes.expected: The interior keeps a warm 2400 to 2700 K glow but shows tonal separation between concrete, fir and leather. The exterior shifts cool.

changes.problem: The frame spends a fifth of its width on a blank neighbour facade, and it never shows the speaker through the glass, so the product cannot be the hero.

evidence.measured: about 22 % of the frame is untextured neighbour. The only speaker visible is about 40 px wide in the vestibule [950,460,990,510].

change.to: about [-8.5, 1.8, 1.45] at [0.0, 3.4, 1.7], 40 mm, verticals kept level. Place the line of sight so an altar or back-bar speaker sits in a clear pane of the main window, not behind a mullion or the lightbox. Crop the neighbour to a sliver at the left.

changes.expected: The shopfront fills the frame. A smoked speaker reads through the glass in the lower or right third, and the neighbour is reduced to an edge.

changes.problem: The speaker is too dark to read from the street. Its tint and the light through its acrylic are invisible.

evidence.measured: lum_median 23.5, b_median 6; the driver at [950,460,990,510] has median 22, with only a pinpoint highlight reaching 178

change.setting: lamps on each Ember speaker; altar spots
change.from: 1.0 W/m2 at 2900 K; altar 2 x 1500 W, 18 deg
change.to: 3.0 W/m2 at 2900 K; altar 2 x 2200 W, cone 22 deg aimed to graze the acrylic cabinet

changes.expected: The cabinet's smoked tint and edge glow read through the glass. The speaker becomes the brightest coloured object after the practicals.

changes.problem: The frosted lightbox is the brightest broad area in the frame and reads as a backlit poster competing with the room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 93.7, against 22.5 for the interior beside it

changes.expected: The lightbox glows softly and evenly, about 2.5x the room rather than 4x. The dancer stays readable and the eye goes into the room.

changes.problem: The door threshold is a flat, evenly lit slab with no texture, the most CG-looking surface in the frame.

evidence.measured: lum_median 146, p5 31, p95 154; uniform, with r193 g138 b84

change.to: honed stone or concrete with visible aggregate, roughness 0.5 and worn edges; tone darkened about 25 %. A brass bowl or doormat edge may break the plane.

changes.expected: The threshold reads as a lit stone step with texture and fall-off rather than a glowing slab.

changes.problem: The street has no life. The flats above are dark and clean, and no one is on the pavement, so it reads as a stage set.

evidence.measured: flats lum_p95 130 with no point above 140: no lit window anywhere above the shop

change.to: two of the flats' windows lit at 2700 K behind sheer curtains (dim, uneven); a bicycle locked to a post or a lone figure at the door, slightly motion-blurred; a couple of figures at the counter visible through the glass

changes.expected: The building is inhabited and the bar visibly open, with some sign of life in the frame.

changes.problem: The sidewalk and kerb are smooth CG planes with no joints, stains or wear.

evidence.measured: lum_range 74 made almost entirely of two reflection blobs and one shadow gradient. At 1:1 there is no paving joint or surface texture.

change.to: SF concrete paving with saw-cut joints about every 1.5 m, gum spots, oil staining and a darker damp band along the kerb, roughness varied 0.35 to 0.8 so the window reflections break up

changes.expected: The pavement reads as a real San Francisco sidewalk. The window's reflection becomes streaky and broken instead of two clean blobs.

out_of_scope.request: Make the speaker in the vestibule larger or give it a stronger tint
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's shape, size and colour are fixed. Only light and camera may bring it forward (c3, c4).

out_of_scope.request: Replace the dancer image in the lightbox or redesign the etched name
out_of_scope.why: The screens, what they show and the shopfront are fixed by the card. Only brightness can change (c5).

out_of_scope.request: Redesign the blackened-steel cladding's tile grid
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront's design is fixed. Its patina may change: raise roughness and even out the flaky specular blotches so it reads as blackened steel, not glazed tile.
